mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months indicates the Federal Reserve is shifting to an easing stance, lowering discount rates and increasing equity valuation sensitivity, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% triggers a risk-off reaction in equity markets, compressing discount rates and reducing the present value of future cash flows, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 2% month-over-month signals a weakening labor market, reducing equity risk premiums and increasing investor demand for safe assets, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns in weakening periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) below 1% month-over-month indicates strengthening labor market conditions, compressing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in strengthening periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 93.2 (as of November 2010) indicates softening domestic demand, compressing discount rates and increasing equity risk aversion, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in softening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 6-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 218.37 (as of November 2010) indicates accelerating inflation, compressing discount rates and reducing equity risk premiums, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in inflation acceleration periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 6-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in retail sales (HOUST) above 610 (as of November 2010) indicates strengthening consumer demand, compressing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in strengthening periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 6-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 9.6% (as of November 2010) signals a stronger labor market, compressing discount rates and increasing equity risk appetite, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in strengthening periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 6-month rolling window.
